title: Signal a lane change to the left with a car's one-touch turn signal: three flashes, the stalk never locked on
keywords: push to a soft stop without passing the detent
instruction: Give the three-flash lane-change signal for a lane change to the left.
context: Every driver signals lane changes with the turn-signal stalk, and every passenger has watched it done. Most cars have a one-touch lane-change signal; a Kia owner's manual: "move the turn signal lever slightly and then release it. The lane change signals will blink 3 times." Pushed further, the stalk clicks into its locked turn position and keeps flashing, telling other drivers a turn that is not coming. The hand skill is a precise, gentle push: pushed 2 cm from its end, the stalk closes its contact after 7.6 mm and passes the crest of its detent at 28 mm, against a spring rising from 1.9 N to 6.3 N; the finger must stop inside that window and let go before the third flash ends, reaching in from above between the wheel's rim (4.3 cm in front) and the column. A stiff, position-controlled arm that pushes 'down until it stops' locks it. One arm does it; the other is not needed.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Steering column section on a bench stand, fixed (a left-hand-drive car's column with its wheel and combination switch): steering wheel 37.2 cm across (2.8 cm grip, three spokes, 15 cm hub) facing the robot, its centre at x 16.5, y -5.0, z 20.5; column shroud 7 cm across from x 19.5 to 47; switch housing at x 23 to 29; wiper stalk on the right; a steel post (x 40.5) and plate (16 x 20 cm) under it. (2) Turn-signal stalk on the switch's left, on a hinge about the x axis at x 26.0, y -0.2, z 18.3: 17 cm long, pointing to +y, 15 deg back toward the robot and 8 deg down, a 19 mm grip on its last 6 cm, its end at x 21.6, y 16.1, z 15.9. Down signals left. (3) Instrument panel behind the wheel, 18 x 7 cm, its face turned 50 deg up, centre x 33, y -5, z 28, with a green arrow 3.2 cm long on each side (y 0 and y -10) that lights with each flash. Both arms start at the ready pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step from the device: the stalk's angle, its switch contacts (closed at 3 deg, open below 2.5 deg) and lock, and the flasher (0.75 s period; at least 3 flashes per signal, more while the contact stays closed or the stalk is locked). 0: no left signal; the right arrow ever flashed (0 for the rest of the run); or the stalk still locked at the end. 0.25: the stalk locked into the left turn position (passed its detent's crest at 11 deg and clicked in at 14 deg) at some point, then returned to rest. 0.5: a left signal without locking, but more than 3 flashes, more than one push, or at the end the stalk not at rest (within 1 deg), still flashing, or a finger within 1 cm of the stalk. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): exactly 3 left flashes from one push, never locked, the stalk at rest, the flasher stopped, every finger 1 cm or more from the stalk. Real trial: count the arrow's flashes on the video (or the flasher's log); a locked stalk stays down when let go.
reset_notes: Wait until the flashing stops; if the stalk is locked, push it back to centre by hand. Check the stalk rests at centre and the wheel is straight (spokes level). Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The column, wheel and switch are boxes, cylinders and capsules at true size; the wheel is fixed (no self-cancelling by turning it). The stalk's spring and detent are a piecewise-linear joint spring updated every control step (angles and forces are estimates of a typical switch). The flasher is the same rule in code (3 flashes per touch, 0.75 s period) and lights a green arrow; there is no sound or relay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper came round the wheel close to the stalk once, about step 900, but did not push it down; both arms spent most of the run near their bases; no arrow flashed); demo: 1.0
